hosts.noResults: No host matches your search. Check the spelling, or clear the search to see every host.

errors.IPC_FORBIDDEN: {{appName}} refused a request from this window. Restart {{appName}}. If it happens again, please report a bug.
errors.IPC_INVALID_PAYLOAD: {{appName}} received a request it could not read. Restart {{appName}} and try again.
errors.INTERNAL: Something went wrong inside {{appName}}. Try again. If it keeps happening, restart the app.
errors.SETTINGS_WRITE_FAILED: Your settings could not be saved. Check that the disk has free space and the settings folder is not read-only, then try again.
errors.VAULT_UNAVAILABLE: Windows could not provide the encryption {{appName}} uses for your saved hosts, so they cannot be opened or saved. Restart {{appName}}. If it keeps happening, sign out of Windows and sign in again.
errors.VAULT_KEY_UNREADABLE: Your saved hosts were encrypted by another Windows account or computer, so they cannot be opened here. Sign in with the account that created them. {{appName}} has not changed the file.
errors.VAULT_CORRUPT: Your saved hosts file is damaged or was changed outside {{appName}}. {{appName}} has not touched it. Close {{appName}}, replace vault.json in %APPDATA%\{{appName}} with the newest copy from the vault-backups folder next to it, and start {{appName}} again.
errors.VAULT_NEWER_VERSION: Your saved hosts were written by a newer version of {{appName}}. Install the latest version to open them.
errors.VAULT_WRITE_FAILED: Your change could not be saved. Check that the disk has free space and the {{appName}} folder in %APPDATA% is not read-only, then try again.
errors.HOST_NOT_FOUND: This host no longer exists; it may have been deleted. Close this window and pick the host again from the list.
errors.KEY_FILE_UNREADABLE: The key file could not be read. Check that it still exists and that your account can open it, then choose it again.
errors.KEY_FILE_EXPIRED: The key file you chose is no longer ready to save. Choose the file again.
errors.KEY_INVALID: This file is not a private key {{appName}} can read. Choose an OpenSSH, PEM or PuTTY (.ppk) private key, not the .pub file.
errors.KEY_PASSPHRASE_REQUIRED: This key is protected by a passphrase. Type the passphrase to use it.
errors.KEY_PASSPHRASE_WRONG: The passphrase does not unlock this key. Check it and try again.
errors.KEY_REQUIRED: Choose the private key file to sign in with.
errors.SESSION_NOT_FOUND: This connection is no longer open. Close the tab and connect again.
errors.SESSION_LIMIT: Too many tabs are open. Close some tabs, then connect again.
errors.SSH_HOST_NOT_FOUND: The server name could not be found. Check the address for typos and that you are connected to the internet or your VPN, then connect again.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_REFUSED: The server refused the connection. Check the port (SSH usually uses 22) and that the SSH service is running on the server, then connect again.
errors.SSH_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE: The server cannot be reached from this network. Check your internet or VPN connection, then connect again.
errors.SSH_TIMEOUT: The server did not answer in time. Check the address and port, and that no firewall blocks SSH, then connect again.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_CLOSED_BY_SERVER: The server closed the connection before sign-in finished. It may only accept some users or IP addresses. Check the server's SSH settings or ask its administrator, then connect again.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_LOST: The connection was lost. Check your network, then connect again.
errors.SSH_HOST_KEY_CHANGED: The server's identity key is not the one you trusted before. Someone may be intercepting the connection, so {{appName}} stopped. If the server was reinstalled or its key was changed on purpose, check the new fingerprint with the server's administrator before you remove the old key.
errors.SSH_HOST_KEY_REJECTED: You did not trust the server's key, so {{appName}} did not connect. Connect again once you have checked the fingerprint.
errors.SSH_AUTH_FAILED: The server did not accept the user name, password or key. Check them in the host settings, then connect again.
errors.SSH_ALGORITHM_MISMATCH: {{appName}} and the server have no encryption method in common. The server may be very old or use unusual settings. Update the server's SSH software or ask its administrator.
errors.SSH_SHELL_FAILED: You are signed in, but the server did not open a terminal. The account may have no shell. Check the account on the server or ask its administrator.
errors.SSH_FAILED: The connection failed for an unexpected reason. Connect again. If it keeps failing, check that the server accepts SSH connections.
errors.QUICK_CONNECT_INVALID: {{appName}} could not read that address. Type it as user@host or user@host:port, then try again.
errors.GROUP_NOT_FOUND: This group no longer exists; it may have been deleted. Close this window and pick the group again.
errors.GROUP_PARENT_INVALID: A group can't go inside itself or one of its own subgroups. Pick another group to put it in.
errors.GROUP_TOO_DEEP: Groups can be nested at most eight levels deep. Pick a group higher up to put it in.
errors.KEY_NOT_FOUND: This key is no longer in the Keychain; it may have been deleted. Choose another key.
errors.KEY_IN_USE: Hosts or identities still sign in with this key. Switch them to another sign-in, then delete the key.
errors.KEY_GENERATE_FAILED: The key could not be generated. Try again. If it keeps failing, restart {{appName}}.
errors.IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND: This identity no longer exists; it may have been deleted. Choose another identity or another sign-in.
errors.IDENTITY_IN_USE: Hosts or groups still use this identity. Give them another sign-in, then delete the identity.
errors.USERNAME_REQUIRED: This host has no user name. Type the user name it signs in with, or choose an identity.
errors.AGENT_UNAVAILABLE: No SSH agent is running. Start the "OpenSSH Authentication Agent" service (Windows Services) or Pageant, add your key, then connect again.
errors.AGENT_NO_KEYS: The SSH agent is running but holds no key. Add your key with ssh-add (or load it in Pageant), then connect again.
errors.KEY_UPGRADE_EXPIRED: This upgrade was started too long ago or already ran. Start it again.
errors.KEY_UPGRADE_NOT_NEEDED: This host already signs in with a key or the agent, so there is nothing to upgrade.
errors.KEY_UPGRADE_INSTALL_FAILED: The server did not accept the command, so the key was not added. Check that the account has a home folder and a POSIX shell, then try again. Nothing was changed on this host.
errors.KEY_UPGRADE_TEST_FAILED: The key was added to the server, but signing in with it did not work. The server may not allow key sign-in (PubkeyAuthentication in sshd_config). This host still signs in with its password.
errors.OPERATION_CANCELLED: You cancelled, so nothing was changed.
errors.JUMP_HOST_NOT_FOUND: The jump host of this host no longer exists; it may have been deleted. Choose another jump host in the host settings.
errors.JUMP_HOST_LOOP: The jump hosts lead back to this host, or there are more than five in a row. Choose a jump host that does not lead back here.
errors.JUMP_FORWARD_FAILED: The jump host did not let the connection through. Check that the next server's address and port are right, and that AllowTcpForwarding is on in the jump host's sshd_config.
errors.PROXY_UNREACHABLE: The proxy could not be reached. Check its address and port and that it is running, then connect again.
errors.PROXY_AUTH_FAILED: The proxy did not accept the user name or password. Check them in the host settings, then connect again.
errors.PROXY_REFUSED: The proxy refused to connect to the server. The proxy may block this address or port. Check the proxy's rules, then connect again.

hostForm.name: Name
hostForm.nameHint: Optional. The address is used when you leave it empty.
hostForm.addressInvalid: Type a host name or IP address, like server.example.com or 203.0.113.7.
hostForm.usernameInvalid: Type the user name you sign in with, like root. Spaces, @ and : are not allowed.
hostForm.passwordAskHint: Leave empty to be asked each time you connect.
hostForm.passwordKeepHint: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
hostForm.passphraseKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the saved passphrase.
hostForm.portInvalid: Use a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.
hostForm.useSessionSignIn: Save the password or key that worked for this connection
hostForm.portInheritHint: Leave empty to use {{port}} from the group.
hostForm.environmentHint: Marks the host so you can tell production servers apart at a glance.
hostForm.tagsHint: Separate tags with spaces or commas, like web eu.
hostForm.tagsInvalid: Use at most {{max}} tags, each one word of up to 50 characters, without #.
hostForm.passphraseStoredHint: Saved in the encrypted vault, so you are not asked again.
hostForm.agentHint: Uses the keys loaded in the Windows OpenSSH agent or in Pageant. The private key never enters Kelidar. Choose which agent in the Keychain.
hostForm.identityRequired: Choose the identity this host signs in with.
hostForm.inheritHint: Signs in as {{username}} with the identity {{name}} from the group. Changing the identity changes every host that uses it.
hostForm.agentForwardHint: Lets this server use your agent's keys to reach other servers. Turn it on only for servers you trust: anyone with root on it can use your keys while you are connected.
hostForm.jumpHostHint: Connect to this server through another saved host. That host can have its own jump host too.
hostForm.jumpDirect: None (connect directly, not through the group's jump host)
hostForm.proxyWithJump: With a jump host, the jump host's own proxy is used for the first connection. Set the proxy on the jump host.
hostForm.startupHint: Typed into the shell right after you sign in, like cd /var/www. Not typed again when a sticky session resumes.
hostForm.startupInvalid: Use one line of at most 1000 characters.
hostForm.stickyHint: Your shell runs inside tmux on the server, so after a dropped connection you continue right where you were. Kelidar checks for tmux and then runs:

prompts.hostKeyBody: This is the first connection to {{target}}. Make sure the fingerprint below matches the one from the server's administrator or hosting provider.
prompts.hostKeyHint: Once trusted, {{appName}} remembers this key and stops the connection if it ever changes.
prompts.passwordRetry: That password did not work. Try again.
prompts.passphraseRetry: That passphrase did not unlock the key. Try again.

terminal.label: Terminal: {{title}}
terminal.forgetKeyBody: Only do this if you know why the server's key changed, for example because the server was reinstalled. {{appName}} forgets the old key for {{target}} and asks you to check the new fingerprint before connecting.
terminal.tmuxMissing: This host uses a sticky session, but tmux is not installed on the server, so a normal shell opened. Work in it is lost if the connection drops.
terminal.tmuxInstall: To install tmux, run one of these on the server (Debian or Ubuntu, Fedora or RHEL, Alpine), then connect again:

quickConnect.hint: For example root@server.example.com:2222, or paste a whole ssh command with -p and -i.

errors.empty: Type a server to connect to, like root@server.example.com.
errors.missing-host: Add the server's address after the @, like root@server.example.com.
errors.missing-user: Add the user name before the address, like root@server.example.com.
errors.invalid-host: The server address is not valid. Use a host name or IP address, like server.example.com or 203.0.113.7.
errors.invalid-user: The user name can't contain spaces, @ or :. Check it and try again.
errors.invalid-port: The port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535, like :2222.
errors.missing-value: {{option}} needs a value after it, like -p 2222.
errors.unsupported-option: {{option}} is not supported in Quick Connect yet. Remove it and try again.
errors.remote-command: Quick Connect opens a terminal only. Remove the command after the address, or put quotes around a path with spaces.
errors.unclosed-quote: A quote is not closed. Add the missing " or ' and try again.

groups.name: Name
groups.nameRequired: Type a name for the group.
groups.defaults: Defaults for hosts in this group
groups.defaultsHint: Hosts in this group and its subgroups use these values unless they set their own.
groups.empty: No hosts in this group yet.
groups.deleteBodyTop: Its hosts and subgroups move to the top level. No host is deleted.
groups.deleteBody: Its hosts and subgroups move to {{parent}}. No host is deleted.
groups.identityHint: Hosts in this group that set neither a user name nor an identity sign in with this one.
groups.jumpHostHint: Hosts in this group connect through this host unless they choose another one or none.

palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Type a host, a command or a setting…
palette.groupPlaceholder: What to do with the group {{name}}…
palette.empty: Nothing matches. Try fewer letters or another word.
palette.footer: Enter runs or connects. Shift+Enter shows more actions for a host. Esc closes.
palette.footerPage: Enter runs the action. Backspace goes back. Esc closes.

commands.duplicateTab: New tab on the same connection

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Every command is also in the command palette.
shortcuts.outsideTerminal: The first key works outside the terminal; the shell uses it inside.
shortcuts.favorite: Add to or remove from favorites
shortcuts.paletteRun: Run, or connect to the host

keychain.title: Keychain
keychain.identitiesBody: A user name with its sign-in, shared by many hosts. Change it once and every host that uses it follows.
keychain.noIdentities: No identities yet. Create one when several hosts sign in as the same user.
keychain.identityBody: Hosts that use this identity sign in as this user, with this sign-in.
keychain.keysBody: Private keys stay in the encrypted vault on this computer. Copy a public key to put it on a server.
keychain.noKeys: No keys yet. Generate one, or import an OpenSSH or PuTTY (.ppk) key.
keychain.agentBody: Hosts set to "SSH agent" sign in with the keys loaded in an agent, and agent forwarding uses it too.
keychain.agentNoneHint: No agent is running. Start the "OpenSSH Authentication Agent" service in Windows Services and add a key with ssh-add, or start Pageant and load a key.
keychain.passphraseMismatch: The two passphrases are not the same. Type them again.
keychain.generateBody: The new key pair is saved in the encrypted vault. Afterwards, copy the public key to your servers, or use Upgrade to key login on a host.
keychain.ed25519Hint: Short, fast and secure. Works with OpenSSH 6.5 (2014) and newer.
keychain.rsaHint: For old servers and devices that do not accept Ed25519.
keychain.passphraseHint: The key is already encrypted inside the vault. A passphrase adds protection when you copy the private key elsewhere.
keychain.importBody: Kelidar copies the private key into the encrypted vault. The file itself is not changed or moved.
keychain.deleteKeyBody: The private key is removed from this computer. Servers that have its public key keep it until you remove it there.
keychain.deleteKeyInUse_one: {{count}} host or identity signs in with this key. Switch it to another sign-in first.
keychain.deleteKeyInUse_other: {{count}} hosts or identities sign in with this key. Switch them to another sign-in first.
keychain.deleteIdentityBody: The identity and its saved password are removed. Its key stays in the Keychain.
keychain.deleteIdentityInUse_one: {{count}} host or group uses this identity. Give it another sign-in first.
keychain.deleteIdentityInUse_other: {{count}} hosts or groups use this identity. Give them another sign-in first.

upgrade.offer: This host signs in with a password. A key is safer and you never type it.
upgrade.title: Upgrade {{name}} to key login
upgrade.body: Kelidar adds a key to {{target}}, checks that it works, and then signs in with it.
upgrade.step1: Sign in once the way this host does today, and run the command you will see next.
upgrade.step2: Sign in again with the key alone, to check it works.
upgrade.step3: Switch the host to the key and remove its saved password.
upgrade.commandIntro: This command runs on {{target}}. It adds the key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys once and sets the permissions SSH needs:
upgrade.passwordStays: Password sign-in on the server stays on, so nothing else changes for you or other users.
upgrade.running: Adding the key and testing it…
upgrade.doneTitle: Done: this host now signs in with a key
upgrade.doneBody: {{name}} signs in with the key {{key}}. Its saved password was removed from this computer.
